scope: Official post-arrival facts shared by all nationalities for D-2 (degree) and D-4-1 (Korean language) students. Country-specific facts live in visa-playbooks.json.

facts.fact: Foreigners who intend to stay in Korea for more than 90 days from entry must apply for alien registration within 90 days of the date of entry.

Apply at the regional immigration office (관할 지방출입국·외국인관서) with jurisdiction over the place of stay; a visit reservation is made on HiKorea (www.hikorea.go.kr). Many universities also file on students' behalf — check the university's international office.
facts.note: The HiKorea detail page names the jurisdictional office; the visit-reservation step and university group filing are stated on university notices, not on this page.

facts.fact: Basic documents: application form, passport, one colour photo 3.5 x 4.5 cm, plus status-specific attachments (for students typically a certificate of enrolment and proof of residence — confirm with the office).
Fee for issuing or reissuing the residence card (외국인등록증 발급 및 재발급): KRW 35,000. Fees are screening fees and are not refunded once the application is accepted.
facts.note: The older HiKorea detail page (dated 2021-04-13) still says KRW 30,000, cash only. The 2026-09 MOJ manual supersedes it. Payment method was not checked.

facts.fact: Students who entered on an e-visa and belong to a TB high-risk country must submit a TB diagnosis certificate at alien registration (instead of at visa application). All 14 Hangyul priority markets are on the MOJ TB high-risk list (35 countries).

items.title: Report a change of address (체류지 변경신고)

facts.fact: A registered foreigner who moves must report the new address within 15 days of moving in, to the city/district/eup-myeon-dong office or the immigration office for the new address. It can also be filed online (HiKorea / Gov24) before the 15 days run out.
facts.note: The easylaw page used is in the foreign-worker section; the rule comes from the Immigration Act and applies to all registered foreigners. Re-check it against the Immigration Act (Art. 36) on law.go.kr.

facts.fact: D-2 students are enrolled as regional subscribers immediately from the date of entry (students who entered before 2021-03-01 were enrolled from 2021-03-01).
D-4 general trainees (including D-4-1 Korean language students) are enrolled on the day 6 months after entry. Only D-4-3 (primary/secondary school students) are enrolled on entry.
On receiving the health insurance card, one month's premium is paid in advance.
Premiums for D-2 and D-4 (general training) holders are reduced by 50% from a base calculated like domestic regional subscribers, with a minimum floor.
2026 monthly premium for international students: KRW 79,320, due by the 25th of each month.
facts.note: The figure comes from a university notice (Sungshin Women's University, posted 2026-03-06), not from an NHIS page. Show it as 'about KRW 79,320/month in 2026', and link students to NHIS (1577-1000) for their own bill.

facts.fact: Non-payment of premiums can count against the student when applying to the Ministry of Justice for stay extensions and other permits.
facts.note: Widely stated on university notices and in the NHIS 2021 notification; the NHIS page wording was not captured in this pass.

facts.fact: Part-time work needs prior permission for activities outside the visa status (체류자격외 활동허가) from the immigration office. The steps are: employment contract (standard contract stating the hourly wage), then a confirmation form written by the university's international-student officer, then an online or in-person application, then permission. D-2 students pay no fee for this permission.
Eligible: D-2-1 to D-2-4, D-2-6 and D-2-7 immediately. D-4-1, D-4-7 and D-2-8 only once 6 months have passed since entry (or since the change of status).

Weekly weekday caps under the general rule (in force since 2023-07). Associate degree, or bachelor's years 1-2, with TOPIK 3 (or KIIP level 3 / Sejong Intermediate 1): 25 h. Bachelor's years 3-4 with TOPIK 4: 25 h. Master's/PhD with TOPIK 4: 30 h. Students who have NOT met the Korean-language standard: 10 h (associate/bachelor) or 15 h (master's/PhD). Degree students who meet the standard have no hour limit on weekends, public holidays and vacations. Certified-university students, students with an A average in the previous semester, and students with TOPIK 5 or higher get 5 extra weekday hours.
facts.note: English-track students can meet the language standard with TOEFL iBT 71, IELTS 5.5, CEFR B2 or NEW TEPS 327. Higher caps (30/35 h) apply only under the regional (광역형) visa pilot, 2025-06-13 to 2026-12-31. Do not show those as the general rule. The manual's sample forms still print older numbers (20 h); the rule table is what counts.

facts.fact: Permission is refused if the previous semester's GPA is below C (2.0), or, for language students, if average attendance is below 90%. Language students (D-4) may hold at most 1 workplace for up to 6 months per permission. D-2 students may hold up to 2 workplaces for up to 1 year.
Weekly hour cap for D-4-1 language students.
facts.note: The rule table in the 2026-09 manual covers degree programs only. A human should confirm the D-4 cap before it is shown.

facts.fact: Barred work includes: manufacturing (unless TOPIK 4 or higher), construction, delivery/rider/gig platform work, dispatch or subcontracted work, remote work, and work against public morals.
Working without permission is punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million, and can lead to deportation.
Screening fee for an extension of stay: KRW 60,000.
A D-2-1 to D-2-4 visa grants a stay of up to 2 years (single entry). A D-4-1 visa grants up to 6 months (single entry). Students extend in Korea before the stay expires.
